content.comment_body: Is there an update for [product_name] software that supports the latest Mac OS 10.15 Catalina, given it only runs 64-bit apps? Thanks, [user_name]
Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. See the attachment for the operating systems currently supported by [product_name] software.

Thank you for your reply, but I have already reviewed that document. Is there any plan to release an update compatible with Mac OS 10.15 Catalina? When is it expected to be available? (The current [product_name] software is not functioning at all with Mac OS 10.15.) Many Mac users rely on [product_name], and now cannot service their customers who use it. Thanks in advance for your feedback.

If your operating system is not one specifically listed, you won’t receive support from [company_name]. They do not test all OS versions. You can, however, submit a Support Request if you want a response directly from [company_name].
It is surprising that a company like [company_name] doesn’t update its software to work with newly released operating systems, such as the Mac OS from Apple (released October 2019).
Try using this device for easier operation: [IMAGE]
[product_name] software is Java-based. The Java version used supports Mac OS X up to 10.11 (and Windows 10), so [product_name] V[version_no] does not offer compatibility with newer releases.
[product_name] software and Java functioned well until Mac OS 10.14.6 (Mojave)...

The issue is Mac OS Catalina (10.15.x) has removed support for 32-bit applications entirely. In previous Mac OS releases, users were warned that programs were not optimized for their Mac and needed updates; this meant 32-bit code was still being used. You may stay on 10.14 temporarily for continued security updates, but it’s generally not recommended to avoid updating for long. If you have a new Mac running Catalina, one workaround is using a Linux virtual machine (like Linux Mint on VirtualBox) and running the Linux version of [product_name] software until [company_name] releases a 64-bit Mac version. This situation is similar to Windows 7’s issues with legacy 16-bit code.

I’m experiencing this problem too. [product_name] software will not run on any of my Macs since updating to Catalina—across several desktops and laptops. Please [company_name], provide a 64-bit compatible version for Mac users.
Hello! Is there already an update for Mac OS 10.15 Catalina? If there is, where can it be downloaded?

Here is the latest statement from [company_name] on [product_name] V[version_no] (from the online help): Supported OS for [product_name] V[version_no]: - Windows: Windows XP, 7, 8, 10 - Mac OS X: 10.7 to 10.11 - Linux: SUSE Linux 11.3 sp3, kernel 3.0.76; compatible distributions must support Java 2 - Java Runtime Environment 1.8.0_121 is recommended ------------------------------------------------------------------- Other Mac OS versions are not tested or supported by [company_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Multiple users are frustrated by the lack of compatibility between [product_name] software and Mac OS Catalina, which only supports 64-bit applications. Without updates, Mac users are unable to operate the software and support their clients. While virtual machine workarounds exist, they are inconvenient and not practical for most. There is disappointment that [company_name] is not keeping pace with operating system updates.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want [product_name] software to be updated so it works with recent Mac OS versions, particularly a native 64-bit version compatible with Catalina and future releases.
